text: The Student Government Association There shall be an organization named the Student Government Association of Stevens Institute of Technology, herein referred to as the “SGA.” The SGA shall promote the welfare of the enrolled undergraduate students of Stevens Institute of Technology, herein referred to as the “Student Body,” and Stevens Institute of Technology, herein referred to as the “Institute,” as a whole. The SGA shall govern the Student Body and represent its interests. The SGA shall have at least one faculty or staff advisor, herein referred to as the “SGA Advisor” whose responsibilities are outlined within the governing documents. All members of the Student Body shall be considered members of the SGA. All mem- bers of the Student Body who have been elected or appointed to positions of the SGA shall be called “Officials of the SGA.” Only members of the Student Body shall be eligi- ble for these positions. No member of the Student Body with a cumulative Grade Point Average of less than a 2.5 shall seek, be appointed to, or maintain a position as part of the Officials of the SGA. Unless specified otherwise, no member of the Student Body shall hold more than one of the positions noted as an Official of the SGA. All members of the Student Body shall pay a Student Activity Fee to the Institute as determined by the Institute in conjunction with the SGA, which shall be delegated to the SGA for allocation. The Student Activity Fee shall fall equally on each member of the Student Body each semester. The SGA shall have the power, within its own means, to recommend a change in the amount of the Student Activity Fee.

The Legislative Branch There shall be a Senate of the Student Government Association, a deliberative assembly whose membership, powers, and responsibilities are defined herein. A Senator is an elected representative of the Student Body. Senators are responsible for and have a duty to represent the interests of their respective constituents. Senators function as equals and have no authority over one another except in the positions outlined in the governing documents of the SGA.

Membership The Senate shall have one seat for every seventy-five (75) students. The number of seats shall be determined by following standard rounding rules. These seats shall be divided between a quantity of “by-School” seats and a quantity of “at-Large” seats. Each school shall have one Senate seat for every one-hundred (100) students enrolled in that school as of the first day of classes of that academic year. The number of seats shall be determined by rounding to the next full hundred. Should a School consist of fewer than one hundred (100) students, it shall have one Senate seat. The remainder of the seats will be assigned the classification of “at-Large” seats.

Sessions of the Senate The session of a particular Senate shall begin at the start of the Senate meeting following the conclusion of the General Senator Elections period held within the first month of the fall semester, and end at the start of the next session of the Senate. A session of the Senate shall be defined separately from the Senate’s parliamentary session. Each session of the Senate shall be numbered, beginning with the first session of the Student Council in April 1913. The Senate of the 2025-2026 academic year shall be the one hundred and eleventh (112th) Senate.

Reduced and Full Session During any period in which either classes are not to be held for more than one week or less than half of the Student Body is enrolled in classes, and the Senate is not in recess, the Senate shall be considered to be “in reduced session.” Attendance at any Senate meeting shall not be mandatory while the Senate is in reduced session. The Senate shall be considered “in full session,” or simply “in session,” at any time that it is neither in recess nor reduced session.

Meetings The Senate shall meet at least once each week while it is in session. Any Senate meeting must either be regularly scheduled as resolved by the Senate, or announced at least three days prior by the Secretary. Two-thirds of Senators shall constitute quorum of the Senate. Senate meetings shall be open to the Student Body. The minutes of Senate meetings shall be made publicly available to the Student Body before the start of the next Senate meeting.

Powers and Responsibilities The Senate shall have the authority to grant the status of Recognized Student Organi- zation to any organization that petitions the Senate for recognition whose constitution does not conflict with the governing documents of the SGA and declared purpose is not indistinguishable from the purpose of any existing Recognized Student Organization, as determined by the Senate. The Senate shall have the power to revoke the status of a Recognized Student Orga- nization that has either failed to appropriately manage its funding or does not comply with its own constitution, the governing documents of the SGA, Institute policy, or any applicable local, state, or federal laws. The Senate shall elect a Speaker to chair meetings of the Senate, who may or may not be a Senator, using a plurality voting system. In the circumstance that a Senator is elected as Speaker, they shall abstain from voting on any business unless the Senate is equally divided or when not presiding in cases of impeachment trials. The Senate shall have the authority to override Presidential vetoes by way of a two- thirds affirmative vote. Furthermore, the Senate shall have the authority to overturn the Vice-President of Operations’ decision to form an ad-hoc committee by way of a two-thirds affirmative vote. The Senate shall have the authority to form its own standing and ad-hoc committees whose membership may include any member of the Student Body. A standing committee must have its definition specified in the Bylaws. The Senate shall have the authority to approve Cabinet appointments by way of a two-thirds affirmative vote. The Senate shall have the authority to declare, due to circumstances in which holding regular meetings and conducting business are not viable, a period in which it shall be considered “in recess,” by way of a two-thirds affirmative vote. While in recess, no business may be conducted nor meetings held by the Senate, except that a meeting may be held to consider a resolution to come back from recess ahead of schedule. The Senate may not declare itself in recess for a period which outlasts the current session of the Senate.

Parliamentarian Constitutional oversight of SGA proceedings shall be the responsibility of a Parliamen- tarian of the SGA. The Parliamentarian shall have the right to review the constitution- ality of all motions brought before the Senate prior to or during their discussion. The Parliamentarian shall not have the power to mandate that a motion to be rescinded. The term for a Parliamentarian shall align with the Session of the Senate. It shall be the responsibility of the President to nominate a Parliamentarian within the next two Senate meetings after the position is declared vacant, and the Senate shall approve the Parliamentarian nomination via a two-thirds affirmative vote. Anyone in the Student Body may be elected to the position of Parliamentarian. Should a Senator be elected as the Parliamentarian, they must resign from the Senate within 48 hours of their ap- pointment to the position of Parliamentarian. The Parliamentarian shall be required to attend all Meetings of the Senate, provided however, that they may accrue up to two absences per academic semester. If they are unable to attend a meeting, they must provide written notice to the Secretary at least 24 hours prior to the beginning of the meeting. If the Parliamentarian arrives after the beginning of a meeting or leaves prior to its completion, then they shall accrue half an absence.

The Executive Branch There shall be a President of the SGA, who shall act as the official representative of the Student Body, and a Cabinet of the SGA, an administrative body which shall be responsible for performing duties assigned by the President relevant to its positions. The President and Cabinet shall have the responsibility to promote the welfare of the Student Body by administrative means.

Membership The Executive Branch shall consist of the President and the Cabinet. The Cabinet shall consist of the Vice-President of Operations, Vice-President of Academic Affairs, Vice- President of Finance, Vice-President of Student Interests, Vice-President of Relations, and Secretary. No person who has not been enrolled at least two consecutive semesters at the Institute shall be President or Vice-President of Operations.

Elections and Appointments The President-elect shall make an appointment to each Cabinet position, with the ex- ception of Vice-President of Operations, between being notified of the results of the Presidential election and taking office. The President and Cabinet shall assume office at 8:00 AM EST on the first day of classes of the spring semester following the Presidential election.
Meetings The Cabinet shall meet at least once each week while the Senate is in session, as well as at the request of the President. The President shall act as the chair of these meetings.

Line of Succession and Vacancies In the event of a vacancy of the position of President, the Vice-President of Operations shall assume the position of President, and the Speaker shall assume the position of Vice-President of Operations pending the election of a new Speaker. In the event of a vacancy of the position of Vice-President of Operations, the Speaker shall assume the position of Vice-President of Operations pending the election of a new Speaker. In the event of a vacancy of a Cabinet position other than Vice-President of Operations, the President shall make a new appointment to the vacant Cabinet position.

President The President shall have the responsibility to act as the official representative of the Student Body. The President shall have the responsibility to sign or veto legislation passed by the Senate. A veto may only be done if the President states the reasons for the veto in written form and makes them available to the Senate within three days after the piece of legislation in question has been passed. Presidential vetoes may be overridden by way of a two-thirds affirmative vote of the Senate. Failure by the President to sign a piece of legislation passed by the Senate shall be considered as an implicit veto. The President shall have the authority to act as the chair of meetings of the Cabinet. The President shall have the authority to call unscheduled meetings of the Cabinet in the case of an emergency. The President shall have the authority to call unscheduled meetings of the Senate in the case of an emergency, except when the Senate is in recess.

Vice-President of Operations The Vice-President of Operations shall have the responsibility to perform all duties of the President in the absence of the latter. The Vice-President of Operations shall have the responsibility to act as the liaison between the Senate and the Cabinet. Unless otherwise specified, the Vice-President of Operations shall have the authority to appoint the chairs of all standing and ad-hoc committees of the Senate, which shall be approved by way of a two-thirds affirmative vote of the Senate, with the exception of standing and ad-hoc committees which have an otherwise specified chair in the governing documents of the SGA. The Vice-President of Operations shall have the authority to form ad-hoc committees of the Senate. The Vice-President of Operations’ decision to form an ad-hoc committee may be overturned by way of a two-thirds affirmative vote of the Senate. The Vice-President of Operations shall have the responsibility to oversee the activities of all standing and ad-hoc committees of the Senate.

Vice-President Of Academic Affairs The Vice-President of Academic Affairs shall have the responsibility to oversee the ac- tivities of all standing and ad-hoc committees of the Senate tasked with improving the Institute’s academics. The Vice-President of Academic Affairs shall have the responsibility to act as a liaison between the SGA and the Institute’s faculty. The Vice-President of Academic Affairs shall attend, or send in place a representative to, meetings of the Faculty Senate and the Student Advisory Board.

Vice-President of Finance The Vice-President of Finance shall have the responsibility to act as a liaison between the SGA, Office of Student Life, and Office of Finance regarding any financial issues surrounding the SGA or Recognized Student Organizations. The Vice-President of Finance shall have the responsibility to manage all financial transactions and records of the SGA. The Vice-President of Finance shall have the responsibility to act as the chair of the Senate Budget Committee. The Vice-President of Finance shall have the responsibility to oversee all expenditures made by standing and ad-hoc committees of the Senate.

Vice-President of Student Interests The Vice-President of Student Interests shall have the responsibility to act as the chair of the Committee on Student Interests. The Vice-President of Student Interests shall have the responsibility to act as the liaison between all Recognized Student Organizations and the SGA. The Vice-President of Student Interests shall have the responsibility to aid in the formation of new Recognized Student Organizations.

Vice-President of Relations The Vice-President of Relations shall have the responsibility to act as the liaison between alumni, external partners, and the SGA. The Vice-President of Relations shall have the responsibility to oversee the activities of all standing and ad hoc committees tasked with improving alumni and external relations. The Vice-President of Relations shall be, or seek election to be, a Student Leader Representative on the Stevens Alumni Association Board of Directors. The Vice-President of Relations shall have the responsibility to maintain an active relationship with all Young Alumni Trustees. The Vice-President of Relations shall oversee the SGA’s gift account and fundraising activities associated while consulting the Vice-President of Finance, and aid Recognized Student Organizations in the creation and stewardship of their respective gift accounts.

Secretary The Secretary shall have the responsibility to record minutes of all meetings of the Senate and the Cabinet. The Secretary shall have the responsibility to act as the chair of the Election Com- mittee, which shall serve to verify the results of all Senate and Presidential elections. In cases where the Secretary seeks election to the position of President, Vice-President of Operations, or Senator, or is promised an appointed Cabinet position, the Senate shall elect another Official of the SGA to chair the Election Committee in their place using secret ballot and a plurality voting system.
Oversight/Impeachment

Oversight Committee There shall be an Oversight Committee responsible for the oversight of all Officials of the SGA. The Oversight Committee shall consist of the Speaker, who shall act as the chair and the number of seats on the committee shall be contingent on the proportion of Senators currently within the SGA with one seat for every ten (10) senators while following standard rounding rules. All seats shall be “at-Large” allowing all Senators an equal chance to be elected to a seat. Voting shall be done through a secret ballot and using a ranked choice voting system.

Initial Proceedings & Disciplinary Actions Any Official of the SGA may bring concerns to the Oversight Committee in regards to any other Official of the SGA who may be in breach of the governing documents of the SGA. The aforementioned Official of the SGA must receive a written reply from the Oversight Committee acknowledging that their concerns have been heard. The members of Oversight Committee shall view evidence against the accused Official at the next Oversight Committee Meeting. Should the latter be impeached, then the Oversight Committee shall, with a two-thirds majority vote, debate upon one of the following disciplinary actions: 1. Request to Resign a) The Oversight Committee shall request via Email that the accused Official resigns from the SGA at the earliest available opportunity. b) Should the Official not wish to resign, then they shall follow the procedure outlined in the next listed disciplinary action. c) If the Official does not respond to the Email acknowledging that they have seen the Email within 48 hours, then they shall be removed from office 2. Warning/Clarification of Role a) The Oversight Committee shall request via Email that the accused Official provides, in written notice, acknowledgment of breaching the government documents of the SGA to all Officials of the SGA along with a notice of how they shall improve themselves. b) Upon deliberation by the Oversight Committee after they have received the letter at the next Oversight Committee meeting, the Oversight Committee shall either drop all charges, strip the Official of any special title, or remove the Official from the SGA. Special titles include appointed committee chairs and elected committee membership. c) If the Official does not respond to the Email within 48 hours acknowledging that they have seen the Email, then they shall be removed from office. 3. Removal from Office a) The accused Official shall be removed from office. Removal from Office re- moves an Official of the SGA from their Official position(s). This disciplinary action is effective immediately. 4. Ban from the SGA a) The accused Official shall be removed from their current position and shall be prohibited from holding Office in the SGA ever again. This disciplinary action shall be effective immediately and last forever. If the accused Official is a member of the Oversight Committee, then the latter Oversight Committee member shall not have a vote. The chair must appoint another Senator of that member’s school as a pro tem member to vote on that member’s disciplinary action. If the accused Official is the Speaker, then the Vice President of Operations shall serve as acting chair of the committee while the Oversight Committee deliberates on a disciplinary action. In this circumstance, the Vice President of Operations may break a tie if the vote to adopt a disciplinary action is divided.

Impeachment Proceedings The Oversight Committee shall impeach an Official by adopting the motion “I move to impeach [“Name”].” The motion to impeach shall have the following characteristics: 1. It can be made only by a member of the Oversight Committee at an Oversight Committee meeting. 2. It can be made only on an Official of the SGA. a) If a member of the Oversight Committee moves to impeach another member of the Oversight Committee, then the latter Oversight Committee member shall not have a vote. The chair must appoint another Senator of that member’s school as a pro tem member to vote on that member’s impeachment. b) If a member of the Oversight Committee moves to impeach the Speaker, then: i. The Vice President of Operations shall serve as acting chair of the com- mittee while this motion to impeachment is debated. ii. The Vice President of Operations shall break a tie if the vote on the motion to impeach is divided. 3. It shall not require a second. 4. It shall not be amendable. 5. It shall be debatable. 6. Adoption of this motion shall require a two-thirds majority. Upon completion of the vote, the Oversight Committee impeaches the Official by charging them with breaching the governing documents of the SGA.

Appeal Impeachment Trial An Official of the SGA who has been impeached may appeal the decision of the Over- sight Committee by trial before the Senate within 48 hours of being notified of their impeachment. The Official must write a formal letter and deliver it to the Speaker and VPO entailing their new goals and how they hope to contribute to the SGA or reasoning as to why they believe their impeachment and/or disciplinary action was not warranted within 48 hours of appealing the decision of the Oversight Committee. Once the letter has been delivered, the Secretary shall include “Impeachment Appeal of [“Name”]” on the agenda for the next Senate meeting. If the letter is delivered within 48 hours of the next Senate meeting, then the Appeal Impeachment shall take place during the following Senate meeting. At the Senate meeting, a motion will be made to discuss the Impeach- ment Appeal in this format “I move to vote on the Impeachment Appeal of [“Name”]”. This motion shall have the following characteristics: 1. It shall require a second. 2. It shall not be amendable. 3. It shall be debatable. 4. Adoption of this motion shall require a simple majority. 5. Voting will be conducted via a closed form. The results of the vote shall be effective immediately. Should the Senate approve the Impeachment Appeal, then all Disciplinary Actions levied by the Oversight Committee on the affected individual will be null.
Recognized Student Organizations
Definition A Recognized Student Organization is any organization with non-exclusive membership granted that status by the Senate or any previously existing system of student gover- nance.

Policies Every Recognized Student Organization must have an executive board, or another simi- larly named board, composed of officers elected by the organization for a term of no more than one year or until their successors are elected. Recognized Student Organizations may also choose to have officers who are not members of an executive board. Officers of a Recognized Student Organization shall not be considered Officials of the SGA. No Recognized Student Organization may preclude any member of the Student Body from being eligible for membership. No Recognized Student Organization may preclude any member of the Student Body from participating in its events or activities, except by means of audition or fair contest for a role. No Recognized Student Organization may require a student to participate in its activities or otherwise remain affiliated with the organization. Recognized Student Organizations must cooperate in investigations of their activity brought forth by the SGA.

Elections There shall be an Election Committee responsible for administering all active elections for the President, Vice-President of Operations, and Senate of the SGA. The committee is responsible for determining, prior to the start of the Fall semester, the timeframe when individuals who seek a position, herein referred to as “Candidates”, are to submit an intention to run in an upcoming election to the Secretary, herein defined as the “Nomination Period”, and the timeframe when members of the Student Body may cast votes, herein referred to as the “Voting Period” for all elections of the SGA. The committee shall also ensure all Candidates follow the Election Rules defined in Section 6.6. of the SGA Constitution.

Senator Elections Once per academic year, a General Election of the Senate will be held within the month of September. The Election Committee shall announce election dates, nomination periods, and event schedules to the Senate. All members of the Student Body shall be notified of the Nomination Period and Voting Period for a General Election of the Senate prior to the start of the Fall semester. During the General Election, all active Senators shall need to win a seat or be vacated from their seats at the start of the new Senate Session. The General Election period shall last for 2 weeks. The first week shall be dedicated to the Nomination Period whereas the second week shall be dedicated to the Voting Period, during which ballots for the “by-School” seats will be accepted. Candidates must submit their intention to run to the Secretary during the Nomination Period. Candidates are eligible to run for only one “by-School” seat, designated at the time of submitting their intention to run. At the conclusion of the Nomination Period, the Election Committee shall, in conjunction with the Office of Student Life, have up to 2 days to determine if the Candidates meet the eligibility requirements to be a Senator as defined by Institute policy or established by resolution of the Senate. This verification period shall not count toward the 2-week election period. Once the eligibility for all Candidates has been verified, the Voting Period shall com- mence. Senators from each school shall be elected by secret ballot by the students in that School using a plurality at-large voting system. Candidates may receive votes only from undergraduate students in the same School as the Candidate. All Candidates are required to obtain 2.5% of the votes from undergraduate members of their School. Any Candidate who fails to meet this requirement will not be allowed election to the Senate during the General Election. During the Voting Period, Candidates cannot change their selected “by-School” seat. If there are more Candidates running than the number of “by-School” seats for their specific school are available, the Candidates, given they meet the number of nominations required, may still compete for an “At-Large” seat during this same election cycle. Any seats left vacant will be designated as “At-Large” seats and will be elected alongside the initially defined “At-Large” seats through Senator Vacancy Elections. If a “by-School” or “At-Large” seat has only one candidate running, the Candidate will automatically be elected unless the “Reopen Nominations” option receives more votes than the candidate. If any Candidate receives less votes than the “Reopen Nominations”, they shall not be elected. At the conclusion of the Voting Period, the Election results must be certified by the Election Committee Chair, after which the results must be announced within 2 days.

Senator Vacancy Elections In the event of a Senator’s resignation or a vacancy of a Senate seat, a vacancy election must be held no later than two weeks after. All Senate seats elected through a vacancy shall be considered “At-Large” seats. If there have been 2 separate vacancy elections, then in the event of at least 10% of Senate seats being vacant, a Senator Vacancy Election must be held. The Election Committee may call additional Senator Vacancy Elections with a two-thirds affirmative vote of the Election Committee. Once a Senator Vacancy Election is called, the Election Committee must host a campaign to promote the election to the Student Body. Once the Election Committee recognizes the need for a vacancy election, the election process must begin within one week. Senator Vacancy Elections shall last one week. The first three days shall be dedicated to the Nomination Period, whereas the remainder of the time will be dedicated to Can- didates gathering fifty votes from members of the Student Body. Candidates shall be elected by secret ballot using a plurality at-large voting system. After the Nomination Period closes, the Secretary, in conjunction with the Office of Student Life, shall have up to two days to determine if the Candidates meet the eligibility requirements to be a Senator as defined by Institute policy or established by resolution of the Senate. This verification period shall not count toward the 1-week election period. The certification of the election results by the Election Committee Chair shall take place immediately after and last for no more than two days. If a Senator Vacancy Election is to be held when the Senate is “in reduced session”, the Senator Vacancy Election procedure must commence once the Senate is “in session”. If there is only one Candidate running for a vacant seat, the Candidate will automat- ically be elected unless the “Reopen Nominations” option receives more votes than the candidate. If any Candidate receives less votes than the “Reopen Nominations” option, they shall not be elected.

Tied Senator Elections If two or more Candidates receive an equal number of votes for any vacant Senate seat, the Election Committee shall have a meeting with the tied Candidates and nominate a Candidate to the position by a two-thirds affirmative vote. This vote must be held by a closed ballot.

Presidential Elections The President and Vice-President of Operations shall be elected together on a single ticket by the Student Body using secret ballot and a plurality voting system. A Pres- idential Election shall occur once per academic year following the conclusion of the General Election. The election period shall last two weeks. The first week is the Nomination Period, where all Candidates must gather signatures from 5% of the Student Body to be consid- ered eligible for the next step. All signatures must be on paper form. At the conclusion of the Nomination Period, the Election Committee Chair, in conjunction with the Of- fice of Student Life, shall have up to five days to determine if the Candidates meet the eligibility requirements to be President as defined by Institute policy or established by resolution of the Senate. Afterwards, all Candidates are required to attend a Nomina- tion Verification Meeting with the Election Committee to discuss election rules, ethical guidelines, responsibilities, and campaign materials. This verification period shall not count toward the 2-week election period. The second week of Presidential Elections shall be dedicated to the Voting Period where Candidates must collect votes from members of the Student Body. Each eligi- ble member of the Student Body may only cast one vote total during the Presidential Election. If there is only one individual running, they shall only win the election pend- ing they receive more votes than the “Reopen Nominations” option. Should “Reopen Nominations” receive more votes than all candidates, the Election Committee will be responsible for setting up another election period within three days. At the conclusion of the Voting Period, the Election Committee Chair and the SGA Advisor shall have up to five days to certify the results of the election. The winner of the election shall be announced at the next available Senate meeting and then to the Student Body the next day. During the Voting Period, the Election Committee, in conjunction with the Office of Student Life, shall be responsible for setting up a: 1. Presidential Debate: A mandatory debate shall be held before the end of the voting period, allowing candidates to present their platforms to the student body. The SGA Advisor will moderate the debate unless determined otherwise by the Election Committee. 2. Vice Presidential Debate: A mandatory debate shall be held before the end of the voting period, allowing candidate perceptive for the specific body. The SGA Advisor will moderate the debate unless determined otherwise by the Election Committee. 3. Meet the Candidates: A mandatory event with the purpose of the student body meeting all the candidates. 4. Any and all other events deemed necessary by the Election Committee These events shall be open to everyone in the Student Body. All candidates are required to attend any event deemed necessary by the Election Committee. In the case of a tie between the tickets which receive the greatest number of votes, the Senate shall choose from among those tickets using secret ballot and a plurality voting system.

Conflict of Interest Should a member of the Student Body choose to become a Candidate in any SGA election or be tapped for appointment to any Candidate’s Cabinet, they shall not be eligible for membership on the Election Committee or to chair it.

Election Rules There will always be the specified option to “Reopen Nominations” during the Voting Period for all elections, unless otherwise noted. Only members of the Student Body in good standing with the Institute may vote in an election. Each eligible member of the Student Body may only cast one vote per Candidate but may vote for as many Candidates as they want unless otherwise noted. Individuals reserve the right to serve as Candidates in multiple elections. All Candi- dates who run for a position and are not elected shall remain eligible for all upcoming elections provided they meet all other requirements. All Candidates are granted permission to use Campaign Materials, or items, both digitally and physically, that may help to promote themselves to the Student Body. No Campaign Materials for Presidential Elections may be posted until the Election Com- mittee holds a Nomination Verification Meeting. Candidates shall be given a Campaign Budget, determined by the Election Committee prior to the start of the Fall semester, which they shall not exceed. All campaigning must be studentrun; no faculty, staff, or external organizations may assist with campaign materials, finances, or endorsements. All Campaign Materials, physical or digital, must be approved by the Election Com- mittee via a majority vote prior to their distribution. Any physical Campaign Materials must be removed within 24 hours after the conclusion of the elections Voting Period. All physical and digital Campaign Materials must follow SGA and Institute ethical guidelines. Candidates must also adhere to the Institute’s posting and digital commu- nication guidelines. No campaigning by any individual may be done using Institute systems unless granted explicit permission by the Election Committee and Office of Stu- dent Life. Social media, ads, posts, and endorsements will always be conducted through personal accounts. Mass emailing through Institute systems is prohibited unless explic- itly allowed by the Election Committee Chair and the SGA Advisor. SGA resources, including email lists, meeting spaces, official SGA social media ac- counts, and financial accounts, may not be used for campaigning. The use of any SGA resources must be explicitly approved by the Election Committee and the Treasurer. Candidates must submit a formal request for any intended SGA resource use, and ap- proval must be documented in writing by the Election Committee Chair. No Candidate may engage in slandering of their opponent, nor may they engage in coercion, intimidation, bribery, or voter suppression. Candidates must meet eligibility criteria as set by SGA Guidelines, which include but are not limited to: 1. Maintaining a minimum GPA as determined by SGA policy. 2. Being enrolled as a full-time student at the Institute. 3. Not being on academic or disciplinary probation at the time of candidacy decla- ration. 4. Meeting any additional criteria set forth by the SGA Constitution or Bylaws. These rules are applicable to the General Election of the Senate, Senator Vacancy Elec- tions, and Presidential Elections unless otherwise specified above.

Violations and Enforcement Violation of campaign rules or election integrity as described in Section 6.6. of the SGA Constitution must be reviewed by the Election Committee. Should the Election Com- mittee determine with a majority affirmative vote that a violation of the rules occurred, they shall contact the SGA Advisor and work with them to classify the violation as either Minor or Severe and impose appropriate repercussions. Should a violation be determined as Minor, the Election Committee shall have the authority to send a warning to the Candidate responsible, suspend the Candidate’s Campaign Materials — both digital and physical —, require the Candidate to submit an apology letter to the SGA, or another punishment as determined by the Election Committee Chair and the SGA Advisor. Should an infraction be determined as Severe, the Election Committee shall have the authority to disqualify the Candidate from the election, ban the Candidate from running in all future SGA elections, suspend them from holding any Executive Board position in any recognized student organization, pending approval from the SGA Advisor, or another punishment as determined by the Election Committee Chair and the SGA Advisor.

Bylaws The Bylaws of the Student Government Association shall dictate the procedures for and the regulation of affairs of the SGA and shall be valid for all intents and purposes of this constitution. No bylaw shall supersede or be inconsistent with this constitution. No procedure or legislation shall supersede any existing bylaws, excluding temporary suspension of bylaws and new bylaws. A new bylaw shall be introduced in the form of a bill.

Amendment of this Constitution The SGA shall open a secret ballot referendum for the ratification of any proposed amendment of this constitution within one week of receipt by an Official of the SGA a petition bearing the signatures of ten percent of the students of each Class or initiative of the SGA itself. These referendums shall remain open for a period of thirty-one (31) days. Amendment of this constitution shall become effective by way of a two-thirds affirma- tive vote of the undergraduate students voting, with a voting quorum of five percent of the Student Body.

Adoption This constitution shall become effective upon ratification by the Student Body by way of a secret ballot referendum as specified in Article VIII and approval by the Office of Student Life. The establishment of this constitution shall abolish any previously existing constitu- tion for the governance of the Student Body. The Student Body shall be hereby bound by this constitution and all rules and regulations brought into effect by its powers.

requirements as per the annually ratified SGA Oversight Committee 
● To work with the Speaker and Cabinet to ensure that all top-down initiatives are

● All members shall have the responsibility to bring an individual up for 
impeachment.

Quorum:

Chairperson, to be present.

The members of the Oversight Committee shall consist of four members, as defined in the Constitution, elected by the Senate, and approved by the Cabinet. Each member of the Oversight Committee shall accept the duties imposed on his or himself by the Senate by accepting one of the chair positions below, as appointed by the Chairperson. The chair positions of the Oversight Committee and their expected responsibilities are as follows: ● Chairperson: Hold a bi-weekly meeting to obtain updates from each Oversight Committee member as well as ensure that they are completing their duties as defined in the latter part of this document. A. Purpose: 
The purpose of The Presidents Council (“The Council”) is to establish a direct 
line of communication between the President of the Student Government 
Association and the leaders (presidents or organizational equivalents) of 
student groups recognized as representing large communities of students. The 
Council shall strive to work together to enhance the lives and promote the ideals 
of the Stevens Student Body and bring together those communities represented 
on The Council. Collaboration between these student groups and governing 
bodies shall serve as an ever-present goal of The Council.

B. Membership: 
The President of the Student Government Association shall act as Chair of The 
Presidents Council. The Membership of The Presidents Council should consist of 
the presidents or organizational equivalents of the following organizations but is 
not limited to the list:

Council and determined by a majority vote. The location and times of meetings 
should be announced to The Council no later than one week before the meeting

the next-highest-ranking available member of their organization. The Chair of 
the Presidents Council should be informed of this as soon as possible.

Preamble 
Recognizing the importance of institutional continuity and the value of alumni engagement, the 
Stevens Student Government Association establishes the Board of Advisors of the Student 
Government Association, herein, referred to as “Board of Advisors” to serve as a strategic 
resource that preserves organizational memory and provides guidance for key initiatives. This 
Board is intended to support the long-term success and vision of the SGA by offering insights 
rooted in experience and connection to the Stevens community.

Article I. Mission and Purpose 
The mission of the Board of Advisors is to preserve institutional memory and offer strategic 
guidance on major SGA initiatives. The Board of Advisors shall be comprised of SGA alumni 
whose backgrounds reflect a range of strengths, including institutional knowledge, personal 
impact, visionary leadership, and a commitment to mentorship. The Board of Advisors shall 
meet regularly as to review the SGA’s long-term vision, upcoming policy agenda, and progress 
on key projects.

Article II. Membership 
2.1. Membership 
The Board of Advisors shall consist of no fewer than four (4) and no more than ten (10) 
members, herein referred to as a “Board Member” or “Advisor”. Board Members hold no formal 
decision-making power within the SGA, existing to guide the organization on its long-term goals 
and strategically plan with its leadership. Board Members are bound by the restrictions set forth 
in this addendum.

citation: Addendum A   Board of Advisors, p. 2, chunk 1

2.2. Terms 
Board Members serve for a standard term of three calendar years, starting at 12:00am on the first 
day of July.

2.3. Appointments 
All appointments and reappointments of Board Members shall take place during a Board of 
Advisors meeting in the month of June. New Board Members shall be nominated and confirmed 
by a majority vote of the existing Board Members. At the conclusion of their term, Board 
Members may be considered for reappointment using the same nomination and confirmation 
process. There is no limit to the number of terms a Board Member may serve.

2.4. Vacancy Terms 
A Board Member confirmed at a non-June meeting shall be considered to have started their term 
as if they were elected at the previous June meeting unless they are filling a seat once held by 
another Board Member, in which case, their term shall end when the previous Board Member’s 
was slated to end.

2.5. Restrictions 
No more than two (2) Board Members may be from the same SGA graduating class year at any 
given time. At least two (2) Board Members should be alumni who graduated ten (10) or more 
years prior to their appointment. This shall only apply when considering the appointment or reappointment of Board Members.

2.6. Suspension of Restrictions 
If, after a good-faith effort to recruit qualified alumni following the restrictions outlined in 
Section 2.5. is followed and no suitable candidates express interest; the Board of Advisors may 
temporarily waive this requirement by a two-thirds vote and approval from the SGA President. 
The waiver must be re-evaluated annually during the June meeting.

Article III. Structure 
3.1. Point of Contact 
The SGA President shall serve as the primary point of contact with the Board of Advisors. The 
SGA President is responsible for communicating updates, coordinating meetings, and ensuring 
the Board of Advisors is kept informed of major developments within the SGA, including but not 
limited to the following: 
1. Changes in leadership including but not limited to changes in Cabinet members, 
commencement of a new Session of Senate, and election of a new Senate Speaker. 
2. Progress of all Cabinet initiatives. 
3. Updates regarding SAF budgeting.

citation: Addendum A   Board of Advisors, p. 3, chunk 2

3.2. Chairperson 
The Board of Advisors shall elect a Chairperson from among its members at the January meeting 
each calendar year. In the event of a vacancy, a Chairperson shall be elected at the next 
scheduled meeting to serve the remainder of the term. The Chairperson shall: 
1. Preside over meetings of the Board of Advisors and coordinate meeting agendas with the 
SGA President. 
2. Serve as the primary liaison between the Board of Advisors and the SGA President. 
3. Lead discussions and facilitate Board of Advisors operations in conjunction with the 
SGA President. 
4. Oversee the onboarding of new Board Members in collaboration with the SGA President. 
5. Serve a one-year term and may be re-elected without limitation. A Chairperson elected in 
a vacancy election will serve until the end of the outlined term. The Chairperson may not 
be elected during their final year as a Board Member.

3.3. Meetings 
The Board of Advisors shall convene at least five (5) times per calendar year. One meeting shall 
occur at the beginning of the calendar-year to (1) elect a new Chairperson, and (2) receive 
presentations from all Cabinet members outlining their initiatives, including a proposed annual 
budget from the Vice President of Finance. Another meeting shall be held in June for the purpose 
of Board Member appointments, reappointments, and internal planning. The SGA President and 
Cabinet shall engage with the Board of Advisors regularly, seeking its insight on strategic 
decisions. Meetings may be held virtually or in person and shall be scheduled by the Chairperson 
of the Board in collaboration with the SGA President. Additional meeting structure and topics 
shall be decided on and outlined in the Bylaws of the Board of Advisors as denoted in Article 
VII.

Article IV. Resignation and Removal 
4.1. Resignations 
Members may resign at any time by providing written notice to both the Chairperson of the 
Board and the President of the SGA. In their written notice, Board Members must specify the 
date of their resignation.

4.2. Impeachments 
Should a Board Member violate any of the rules outlined in this addendum or additional 
governing documents for the Board of Advisors, they are subject to impeachment. Any Board 
Member or Cabinet member may raise an impeachment against any Board Member. All raised 
impeachments shall be directed to the President of the SGA who will then call for a meeting to 
discuss it with the Board of Advisors. The Board of Advisors may vote to remove an impeached 
official with a 4/5 affirmative vote.

4.3. Vacancy Nominations 
In the event of a resignation or removal, the Chairperson of the Board, in consultation with the 
President, may call for the appointment of a replacement Board Member.

Article V. Operations and Procedures 
5.1. Quorum 
A majority of Board Members shall constitute a quorum for all meetings.

Board and made available to the entirety of the SGA no later than one week after the conclusion

Article VI. Code of Conduct 
Board Members are expected to uphold the SGA values in all interactions with members of the 
SGA and the Stevens community. All discussions, especially regarding student concerns or 
internal conflict resolution, shall be treated with discretion and professionalism. Board Members 
may not use their position for personal or political gain.

Article VII. Bylaws of the Board of Advisors 
The Board of Advisors shall be provided with a set of Bylaws by the SGA to be approved by the 
Senate through a piece of legislation with a majority vote. The Bylaws of the Board of Advisors 
may be edited following the amendment process listed within them. The Rules Committee of the 
SGA shall check all amendments to the Bylaws of the Board of Advisors to ensure there are no 
conflicts between the amendment and any existing governing documents of the SGA. No rule 
defined in the Board of Advisors Bylaws, or any other governing document of their creation may 
supersede or be inconsistent with the rules outlined in this addendum.

These Bylaws govern the internal operations of the Board of Advisors of the Student 
Government Association. The Board exists as an advisory body to the Student Government 
Association, with authority and structure defined in the official Addendum to the SGA Bylaws. 
These Board of Advisor Bylaws are intended to complement the Addendum and provide 
additional detail for the Board's operations, logistics, and internal governance.

Article II. Nominations and Appointments 
2.1. Initiation 
The Board shall initiate the appointment process of New Board Members no later than May 1 
each year in preparation for the June meeting.

2.2. Application Form 
An open call for applications shall be distributed to the SGA alumni network, graduating SGA 
class, and relevant campus stakeholders. This application period must remain open for a 
minimum of two (2) weeks. Applicants must submit a resume and a brief statement of interest 
outlining their qualifications and SGA involvement. The Board may choose to conduct 
interviews or request additional materials.

outlined in the SGA Board of Advisors Addendum. The Board shall review its Bylaws at least

Article II. Standing Subcommittees 
Section 2.01 Definition 
The CSI shall consist of standing subcommittees. Each subcommittee shall be 
grouped into a category that is then headed by a SC. These subcommittee groups 
include: 
1. Culture, Religion & Faith 
2. Arts & Music 
3. Club Sports, Recreational, Electronics & Gaming 
4. Professional Societies 
5. Non-RSO, Media 
6. Service, Special Interests 
7. New Organizations 
8. Inactive 
There shall be an exemption made to the New Organization and Inactive categories. The 
New Organization subcommittee shall be chaired by the AVPSI. The Inactive subcommittee 
shall be chaired by the VPSI. Neither of these SCs nor subcommittees shall be subject to any 
of the standard subcommittee requirements outlined in this document.

Section 2.02 Composition 
Each subcommittee shall consist of representatives from all RSOs within their category. 
Each RSO within the subcommittee’s category must send at least one(1) representative, as 
determined per the individual RSO’s Constitution. If not explicitly defined in an 
organization’s Constitution, at least one(1) member of their EBoard must serve as a 
representative and attend the subcommittee meeting.

The subcommittees’ primary purpose is to mentor, oversee, and communicate with all 
RSOs within their purview. The responsibilities of the subcommittees shall include but 
not be limited to the following: 
1. Coordinate initiatives across all their represented RSOs 
2. Foster engagement and interest in their represented RSOs 
3. Liaison between their represented RSOs and the CSI, the VPSI, and the 
administration

VPSI, AVPSI, and CCC at the beginning of each semester. Should it be deemed necessary,

● Other initiatives and topics of discussion as decided by the officers of the CSI

The subcommittee meetings shall operate on at least a bi-weekly basis, with the time being 
set by the CCC at the beginning of each semester. Should it be deemed necessary, there may 
be emergency meetings scheduled, with at least seventy-two(72) hours notice being given 
to the SCs. These meetings shall be chaired by the CCC.

The purpose of these meetings shall be outlined as follows: 
● For SCs to provide reports and updates 
● To keep track of SC requirements and establish timelines 
● Plan organization-related initiatives and events

Lead

Definition

Interview 
Once this New Organization Request Form is complete, voting will occur as outlined below. 
Afterwards, a meeting will be scheduled between the proposer, the AVPSI, and a staff 
member from the Office of Undergraduate Student Life. This meeting will be roughly fifteen 
(15) minutes long, and will involve basic questions about the applying Student

● The individuality of the organization 
● The mission statement of the organization 
● The potential student interest for the organization 
● The legality of the organization, and 
● The expected on-campus effects of the organization

The proposed organization shall be voted on during two points. The first vote shall take 
place after the submission of the Request Form, and either the AVPSI, or staff member must

parties vote against approval in the first stage or if at least one party votes against approval 
in the second stage.

Article I: General Provisions 
Purpose 
• This document establishes the rules and procedures governing all elections 
conducted by the Student Government Association (SGA), including General 
Elections, Vacancy Elections, Campaign Regulations, and Presidential Elections. 
Authority 
• The Election Committee is responsible for overseeing and enforcing this Election 
Code. 
• The Secretary is responsible for coordinating election logistics and verifying 
election results. 
Eligibility to Vote and Run 
• All students in good standing with the university are eligible to vote in SGA 
elections. Candidates must meet eligibility criteria as set by SGA guidelines, which 
include but are not limited to: 
I. Maintaining a minimum GPA as determined by SGA policy. 
II. Being enrolled as a full-time student at the university. 
III. Not being on academic or disciplinary probation at the time of candidacy 
declaration. 
IV. Meeting any additional criteria set forth by the SGA Constitution or Bylaws.

Article II: Senator General Election Procedures 
Section 1: Frequency of Elections 
General Elections of the Senate shall occur once per academic year during fall semester. 
• The Election Committee shall announce election dates, nomination periods, and 
event schedule to the Senate. The Senate shall inform the student body. 
• General Elections must be announced by the first day of classes 
• All election dates must be set before the start of the semester to allow for 
advertising at events such as the Flock Party and Pre-Orientation events.

Section 2: Election Process • The election period shall last two weeks in total. • Candidates must submit their intent to run to the Secretary within the intent to run period, which spans the first week of the election period. • The voting period shall last one week, following the conclusion of the intent to run period. • Candidates must obtain votes from 2.5% of students in their respective school, based on the number of undergraduate students in the school. • Only votes that originate from the same school as the candidate will be considered valid. • The option to reopen the intent to run form shall always be included in the election poll. • If any candidates receive fewer votes than the option to reopen the intent to run form, those candidates shall not be elected. • Of the remaining candidates, those receiving the most votes will fill the vacant seats. • Any candidate who fails to be elected may still run in future elections. If a position has only one candidate running, the candidate will automatically be elected unless the 'Reopen Nominations' option receives more votes than the candidate. If 'Reopen Nominations' receives more votes, the seat will remain unfilled until a

will automatically be elected unless the 'Reopen Nominations' option receives more votes than the candidate. If 'Reopen Nominations' receives more votes, the seat will remain unfilled until a future vacancy election. Section 3: Verification • After elections close, a Candidate Verification Meeting will be held by the Secretary and the Election Committee. • The Secretary, in conjunction with the Office of Student Life, shall have up to five days to determine if the nominees meet the eligibility requirements to be a Senator as defined by Institute policy or established by resolution of the Senate. • The Secretary will verify that the votes received are valid once the election period has passed. Section 4: Announcement of the Results • If the election closes on a Sunday night or Monday morning, verification should be completed by Wednesday. • Election results must be announced by Wednesday, ensuring that newly elected Senators can attend the following Sunday Senate meeting.

Section 5: Tie Breaking Procedures 
• In the event that two or more candidates receive an equal number of votes for a 
vacant Senate seat, the tie-breaking procedure shall be implemented as follows: 
• The Election Committee shall notify the tied candidates of the tie and the 
impending tie-breaking process. 
• The Election Committee shall hold a meeting to determine the Elected 
Candidate by a discussion and a unanimous vote. 
▪ In the event the election committee cannot come to a conclusion, the 
Senate shall hold a closed-form vote to determine the winner. 
• A simple majority vote is required to break the tie and 
determine the winning candidate. 
• The non-elected candidate can rerun during the next vacancy and or general 
election.

Article III: Senator Vacancy Election Procedures 
Section 1: Initiating Vacancy Elections 
• Vacancy elections shall occur only for at-large seats in the event of a Senate vacancy 
or resignation. 
• There must be a minimum of 2 vacancy elections. If, after that, there are still seats 
vacant: 
• It is up to the discretion of the Secretary to run an election or when the 
number of vacant seats hits 8% an additional election must occur the 
following week. 
• Once the Election Committee recognizes a vacancy, the election process must begin 
within one week. 
Section 2: Vacancy Election Process 
• The Election Committee shall run a publicity campaign before or during the 
nomination period. 
• The Secretary shall work with the Office of Student Life and relevant university 
administrators to ensure election procedures are properly followed and that results 
are validated. 
• The Election Committee shall announce the election timeline to the Senate, which

Article V: Campaign Regulations & Enforcement 
Section 1: General Campaign Rules 
• No campaign materials (posters, handouts, social media posts, etc.) may be 
publicized before the required Nomination Verification Meeting. 
• No candidate shall engage in coercion, bribery, intimidation, or voter suppression. 
• Candidates must not slander opponents. 
• Candidates must adhere to the university's posting and digital communication 
guidelines. 
• Spending Limits: Campaign budgets must not exceed a set limit in negotiation with 
the candidates and determined by the Election Committee. 
• Candidates must submit a budget to the Election Committee. 
• Campaigns must be student-run; no faculty, staff, or external organizations may 
assist with campaign materials, finances, or endorsements.

Section 2: Campaign Materials & Digital Campaigning • All campaign materials must be approved by the Election Committee before distribution. • Physical campaign materials (flyers, posters, handouts, etc.) must follow university posting policies. • Digital Campaigning Rules: • Candidates may use social media but must follow SGA and university ethical guidelines. • Mass emailing through university systems is prohibited unless explicitly allowed. • Social media ads, endorsements, or posts must be made using personal or student-run accounts. • SGA resources, including email lists, meeting spaces, official SGA social media accounts, and financial accounts, may not be used for campaigning. The use of any SGA resources must be explicitly approved by both the Election Committee and the Treasurer. Candidates must submit a formal request for any intended SGA resource use, and approval must be documented in writing. Section 3: Removal of Campaign Materials • All physical campaign materials must be removed within 24 hours of the election period closing. • Any candidate failing to remove their materials may face a minor election infraction.
